compiled_state.title: Create schema-compliance integration test for PR-80 verification run
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Testing Mode
GREEN

## Story DD Coverage
This task is responsible for satisfying the following story done definitions:
- DD1: runner.py is invoked against the PR-80 diff fixture and the resulting findings JSON contains zero entries with type: "parse_error" (synthetic schema_error)
- DD2: 100% of non-synthetic findings in the output have non-empty cited_excerpt (≥5 chars) and, where severity ∈ {critical, important, fragile}, a reachability field ≥20 chars

## What
Create `tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py` as a new `@pytest.mark.integration` test file that invokes `runner.py` against the PR-80 diff fixture and asserts schema compliance. This IS the one-shot verification run described in the story — the test file is the verification artifact, not a test of new behavioral source code.

The story explicitly scopes OUT unit tests; this integration test verifies the user-visible outcome after S-A (4425-a483), S-B (394e-d81b), and S-C (771d-7c6b) changes are applied.

## Test Approach

### Test 1: test_pr80_zero_synthetic_schema_errors
- **Given**: PR-80 diff fixture at tests/fixtures/ci-review-corpus/pr-80.diff; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set; S-A/S-B/S-C changes applied to runner.py
- **When**: runner.py is invoked as subprocess with DSO_CI_REVIEW_DIFF_PATH=pr-80.diff
- **Then**: findings JSON contains zero entries with type="parse_error"
- Skips if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is absent (pytest.skip)

### Test 2: test_pr80_100_percent_schema_compliance
- **Given**: same as above
- **When**: runner.py invoked as subprocess, real LLM call produces findings
- **Then**: (a) every non-synthetic finding has cited_excerpt with len ≥ 5 chars; (b) every finding with severity in {critical, important, fragile} has reachability with len ≥ 20 chars
- Skips if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is absent (pytest.skip)
- Non-synthetic = finding where type not in {specialist_error, fallback_exhausted, parse_error}

Both tests can share a single runner.py invocation result if memoized or use the shared output; alternatively each test runs independently (acceptable since integration tests may each call the LLM once). Mark both with @pytest.mark.integration.

## Implementation Steps
1. Create file `tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py`
2. Follow the @pytest.mark.integration pattern from test_integration_full_loop.py:
   - Module docstring explaining purpose
   - Import pytest, os, subprocess, sys, pathlib
   - Define FIXTURE_DIFF_PR80 = REPO_ROOT / "tests/fixtures/ci-review-corpus/pr-80.diff"
   - Define _SYNTHETIC_TYPES = {"specialist_error", "fallback_exhausted", "parse_error"}
3. Write test_pr80_zero_synthetic_schema_errors() with @pytest.mark.integration
4. Write test_pr80_100_percent_schema_compliance() with @pytest.mark.integration
5. Add .test-index entry: `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py: tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_runner_smoke.py, tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py`
   (append to existing entry, which already maps runner.py to test_runner_smoke.py)

## File Impact
| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py` | Create |
| `.test-index` | Modify (append test_schema_compliance_pr80.py to runner.py entry) |

## Note on .test-index fuzzy match
Source basename: "runner.py" → normalized: "runnerpy"
Test basename: "test_schema_compliance_pr80.py" → normalized: "testschemacompliancepr80py"
"runnerpy" is NOT a substring of "testschemacompliancepr80py" → .test-index entry is required.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Unit tests pass (exit 0)
  Verify: REPO_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) && python -m pytest tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py -m "not integration" -x 2>&1 | tail -5
- [ ] Lint passes (exit 0)
  Verify: ruff check tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py
- [ ] Format check passes (exit 0)
  Verify: ruff format --check tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py
- [ ] Test file exists at expected path
  Verify: test -f $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py
- [ ] Test file contains exactly 2 integration test functions
  Verify: grep -c "@pytest.mark.integration" $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py | awk '{exit ($1 < 2)}'
- [ ] test_pr80_zero_synthetic_schema_errors function exists
  Verify: grep -q "def test_pr80_zero_synthetic_schema_errors" $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py
- [ ] test_pr80_100_percent_schema_compliance function exists
  Verify: grep -q "def test_pr80_100_percent_schema_compliance" $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py
- [ ] Each test skips when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is absent (pytest.skip present)
  Verify: grep -q "pytest.skip" $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py
- [ ] Test references PR-80 diff fixture path correctly
  Verify: grep -q "pr-80.diff" $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py
- [ ] .test-index entry updated to include test_schema_compliance_pr80.py for runner.py
  Verify: grep "test_schema_compliance_pr80.py" $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.test-index
- [ ] Integration test runs without collection error when API key is absent (collection = skip)
  Verify: python -m pytest tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_schema_compliance_pr80.py --collect-only 2>&1 | grep -v "ERROR\|error"

## Retry Budget
MAX_ATTEMPTS: 3 (sonnet model)
On 3 consecutive sonnet failures: escalate to opus with full diagnostic context (all 3 failure messages)
On 3 consecutive opus failures (6 total): escalate to user with full failure history
If MAX_AGENTS: 0 at sonnet→opus escalation time: skip opus step, escalate to user immediately

comments.body: AC amendment: Both test_pr80_zero_synthetic_schema_errors and test_pr80_100_percent_schema_compliance must assert that runner.py exits with code 0 (not just that the findings JSON has zero parse_error entries). A non-zero exit code indicates runner.py itself detected a schema error or failure — the test should capture returncode from subprocess.run and assert returncode == 0 as the first assertion, before parsing findings JSON. This verifies the full success path including S-A/S-B/S-C's validation and correction logic. Add to each test: assert result.returncode == 0, f'runner.py exited {result.returncode}: stderr={result.stderr}'
